requirements.statement: A feature is re-audited only when the previous round found a true product defect, and at most twice; after that it closes, with anything left named as caveats

Test-only gaps (a missing or weak test, with no product defect) are still fixed, in the same fix pass as everything else, but they never cause another audit: the feature closes with them fixed, or named as caveats if a fix fails

A re-audit builds on the previous one: when the TRD is unchanged since the previous round, it reuses that round's requirement list, and its verifiers check what changed since the previous audited commit plus that report's open items first
A fix run that closes an audit finding fixes every instance of that weakness across the feature, not only the one the audit named
A scheduled wake-up for an audit that already finished does nothing; it never starts a new audit

tasks.description: Create `packages/core/lib/audit-rounds.js` with `classify`, `record(stateDir, round)` append-only writer, `readRounds(stateDir)`, `decide`, `staleWake`, and CLI. Mirror to `.claude/lib/` and symlink `packages/full/lib/audit-rounds.js`. Jest tests for classify, decide (all rounds including cap), reopened features, staleWake, and one-active-trip sequence.

In `packages/core/workflows/audit-build.js`: split `action`'s `gap` into `gap-unbuilt` and `gap-untested` (required), update traceability prompt; reconcile stage returns `handoff` with no class; both return paths carry `handoff` and `index`; accept `args.previous` and `args.trdHash` for requirement-list reuse and scope limiting to changed files and previous open items.

In `packages/core/commands/audit-build.md`: classify handoff items, count defects/gaps/uncovered, record round, call `decide()`; record handed-off items as discoveries and chain `/implement-trd --reconcile --chained`; on close write close record, commit, open PR, print banner with caveats; on re-audit pass `previous`; every wake-up carries run id and checks for stale; readout names round and re-audit/close reason; NEXT names audit only on re-audit. Add `/audit-build` to `implement-trd.md` §3.7 as chained caller.

In `packages/core/lib/discovered.js` `promoteToTrd()`, rows from `foundBy: 'audit-build'` add instruction to find and fix every instance of the weakness across feature's touched files and list each one fixed. Say the same in `implement-trd.md` §2.1a.

In `docs/reference/other-commands.md` and `docs/reference/implement-trd.md`, describe round cap, defect vs test-gap split, re-audits building on previous round, chaining with `--chained`, and stale-wake rule.

Per Owner rulings 1–2 in `packages/core/lib/audit-rounds.js`: at cap with defects, return `chain: true, close: false, reaudit: false, capReached: true` (feature stays open); `classify()` returns `test-gap` for any `test-quality` finding regardless of `action`; `staleWake()` matches by run id only, dropping same-commit rule.

Per Owner rulings 2–3 in `packages/core/workflows/audit-build.js`: test-quality verifier told weak/missing test matters only if masks defect (report as that defect under verification/traceability, not test-quality); when `previous` set, limit verifiers to defect-fixed checks and changed-files scope, with `outOfScope` list separate from findings; TRD hash covers only Objectives and Master Task List sections.

Per Owner rulings 1 and 3: when `capReached`, readout says feature stays open with defects named and NEXT is owner's call (not audit); on re-audit, `outOfScope` items recorded as non-blocking discoveries and listed, never chained. Update reference docs and command surface assertions.

could_not_verify: A real feature converges in at most three audits — Needs a live run on a real feature; the tests prove the decision table and the one-active-trip sequence, not an audit's behaviour
Verifiers choose `gap-unbuilt` versus `gap-untested` correctly — Model judgement; the prompt asks for it, the tests check only the schema

A weak test that hides a real defect is reported as that defect (Owner ruling 2) — Model judgement: the test-quality verifier is told to report the masked defect; the tests check only that the prompt says so
open_questions: OQ-1: When the cap is reached with defect fixes not yet re-audited, should the feature close with a caveat, or stay open for you? — Answered by the owner, 2026-10-01: stay open. 'We don't close with a caveat if there are true defects open.' See AMEND-001
OQ-2: Under `--chained` the fix run skips functional verification. Is that acceptable for audit-chained fixes? — Yes: a re-audit checks defect fixes, and test-gap fixes are themselves tests
